author: The Fortune Teller
title: Technology: Nothing (Good) To See Here
text:
The performance of global equities ( IVV , VTI , VOO , VEA , EFA , IEFA , VWO ) in 2018 is nowhere near what we've seen in 2017.
2017 was an all-green year, with almost every market investors put money into delivering double-digit positive returns.
2018, thus far, is an almost all-red year, with almost every market investors put money into delivering double-digit negative returns.
Small caps are already in negative territory on a YTD total return basis, with large caps barely in the green.
SPY Total Return Price data by YCharts
The US major indices ( SPY , DIA , QQQ , IWM ) are down between ~10% and ~15% since their respective highs.
Symbol Current Level Highest Level / Date Change SPY 265.02 293.94 / September 20th, 2018 -9.84% DIA 269.28 244.65 / October 3rd, 2018 -9.15% QQQ 160.37 187.53 / October 1st, 2018 -14.48% IWM 148.03 173.39 / August 31st, 2018 -14.63% The sharp declines this year are especially felt among the hottest sector - technology ( XLK ). The Nasdaq index has dropped to its lowest since April.
The sector/index's flagship stock, Apple ( AAPL ), is down circa 25% since its all-time high (at $233.47) set on October 3, 2018.
50 days = a loss of ~$280B in market cap.
AAPL data by YCharts
Apple's 25% drop is nothing compared to what happened to one of Wall Street's tech darlings - Nvidia ( NVDA ).
A 55.5% drop - from $292.76 on 10/2 to $133.31 on 11/20 - for a company that had a market cap of nearly $180B is another unprecedented loss of value.
NVDA data by YCharts
But neither Apple nor Nvidia is alone out there.
Tech's popular FAANG stocks have lost more >$1T of their combined market caps. We are still far away from being anywhere a Dot-Com crash 2.0, but a $1T loss, out of only five stocks, in a matter of only seven weeks, is certainly something we've never seen before.
When the unicorn masters of Silicon Valley start putting most of their own money into cash, that may be a sign something bad is happening in the markets.
Investors get pickier, startups get anxious, home prices drop.
It’s no longer business as usual.
Below is perhaps the most disturbing chart for all tech enthusiasts.
If history repeats itself, there is nothing to earn investing in FANG stocks in years to come.
Nonetheless, in the digital age, clocks may be ticking differently.
Only time will tell, but truth is we are likely to remain underweight tech. When we combine the risk and (potential) reward of the sector - we believe there are better places/sectors to put money to work in than this one.
